title: GeoFence Gateway: enforce EU-only residency with tier-aware routing & graceful model fallback
creator: Aditi Menon
description: Implement a GeoFence Gateway service that enforces EU-only data residency rules while performing tier-aware routing and orchestrating graceful fallback to compliant model variants when capacity or matching variants are unavailable. The gateway should support customer-level allowlists/denylists and a cascading decision path that prefers strict residency, then same-region compatible tiers, then controlled cross-region fallback only if the customer is permitted.
background: Several recent compliance audits and customer requests require a deterministic enforcement point for residency, not just policy evaluation. Existing policy engines provide decisions but routing is currently scattered across proxies and load balancers. This causes inconsistent enforcement and makes rollbacks and audits difficult. The GeoFence Gateway centralizes decision enforcement and supplies structured routing metadata to the serving runtime for consistent fallbacks.
goals: 1) Centralize residency enforcement for EU-only customers. 2) Ensure predictable tier routing (hosted vs dedicated vs private) respecting customer allowlists/denylists. 3) Provide automated, observable fallback to compatible model variants with minimal quality regression. 4) Emit audit-ready events for every decision and allow easy policy updates.
acceptance_criteria: Requests labeled ‘eu_residency:strict’ are never routed outside EU unless the customer is allowlisted
Gateway returns structured route decision including chosen region, tier, model_variant, and fallback_reason
When preferred model is unavailable, gateway selects next-best compliant variant per the Variant Fanout Matrix and annotates token-quality-risk in decision metadata
Audit logs contain immutable decision_id, customer_id, policy_version, and timestamp and are queryable within Console -> Compliance
E2E latency added by gateway < 8ms p95 under normal load; end-to-end SLO impact measured and documented
Feature toggle exists to enable/disable soft cross-border fallback per tenant
Unit/integration tests cover allowlist/denylist precedence, emergency deny, and stale-policy handling
tasks: Design API contract for GeoFence Gateway decision endpoint (proto + JSON schema)
Implement policy matcher that accepts tenant metadata, request headers, and consent flags
Integrate customer allowlist/denylist store and cache with 1-minute TTL and change-feed invalidation
Implement Variant Fanout Matrix algorithm: score variants by compliance, latency, cost, and quality
Add audit logging pipeline (structured events to Kafka -> compliance topic) and Console integration
Create runtime adaptor in serving layer to interpret gateway decisions (region pinning, model TTLs, KV cache affinity)
Performance test harness and run baseline + burst scenarios
Write migration runbook and rollback steps for incorrect policy pushes
implementation_notes: Gateway will live in control-plane tier but run regional replicas within EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1) for low-latency enforcement
Policy engine output: {decision_id, policy_version, allowed_regions, permitted_tiers, preferred_variants, fallback_matrix}
Variant scoring favors same-region quantized variants; fallback weight penalizes increased egress risk and model quality delta
Use existing KMS to sign decision_id tokens for audit tamper-proofing
Cache allowlist/denylist in a local in-memory store with subscription to the central config service to minimize RPCs
Serving runtime to implement per-request routing hooks that accept signed decision token to avoid separate lookups
Soft fallback behavior: annotate response header X-Redwood-Fallback-Risk and emit metric fallback_quality_risk{tenant, variant_from, variant_to}
api_contract_changes: POST /v1/routing/decide -> input: tenant_id, request_metadata; output: region, tier, model_variant, decision_token, fallback_reason (optional)
Decision token is a signed compact JSON with decision_id and expiry to be forwarded to serving runtime
Add new optional request header X-Redwood-Decision-Token to API surface for private/dedicated routing paths
rollout_plan: Feature-gate rollout: enable for internal test tenants in staging first
Phase 1: staging + 5 internal tenants; collect latency and decision correctness metrics
Phase 2: pilot with 3 customers flagged by Compliance; enable audit log forwarding
Phase 3: open opt-in for all EU customers; monitor fallback rates and token-quality-risk metrics
Phase 4: default-on for tenants with eu_residency:strict after two weeks of zero regressions
Emergency rollback: set emergency_block_mode to deny all cross-border fallbacks and fall back to pre-gateway routing via control-plane flag
test_plan: Unit tests for policy precedence (denylist > tenant policy > org-level allowlist)
Integration tests simulating model pool exhaustion and verifying chosen fallback variant
Chaos test: kill regional gateway replica and validate failover to other EU replica without policy drift
Performance: synthetic traffic ramp to measure p50/p95 added latency and routing throughput
Compliance validation: verify audit events contain required fields and signature verification in Console
blockers: Final policy precedence semantics pending legal review for emergency allowlist overrides
Need compliance sign-off on audit retention window and encryption-at-rest for Kafka topic
